finding.claim: GET /rss passes the attacker-supplied query parameter u directly to URI.open, letting an unauthenticated caller make the server fetch arbitrary http/https/ftp URLs (including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints) and read the first 400 bytes of the response.
finding.source: params[:u] query parameter on GET /rss (app.rb:7-8), no authentication
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8; response returned via data[0, 400] at app.rb:9

trace.note: get "/rss" route accepts any unauthenticated request
params[:u] passed unmodified to URI.open, which performs the outbound request and follows redirects to any host
first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: None on this path: no scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no redirect re-validation, no port restriction, no timeout, no body-size cap. Adjacent non-SSRF concern (unverified, Ruby-version dependent): URI.open falls back to Kernel#open for strings without a scheme, enabling local file read and possibly pipe command execution; should be reviewed separately.

verdict.reason: app.rb:7-8 takes params[:u] unauthenticated and passes it unmodified to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns data[0, 400]; the only host allowlist (TRUSTED, app.rb:5, checked at app.rb:14) guards the separate /trusted route, not /rss, so nothing on the /rss path closes the SSRF.
